recommended_sources.rationale: Provides >=3 independent university donors per profile, combining quantitative interiorscape lux/FC, pH, and NPK data (UF/IFAS) with practical apartment watering and dormancy rules (UW-Madison, Clemson, NC State).
Covers 39/40 target condition_ids with scientifically validated differential diagnostics, symptom keys, and non-chemical IPM action steps.
Separates cat vs. dog toxicity and identifies the exact toxic principle (e.g., insoluble calcium oxalates, saponins, cardiac glycosides) for manual fact verification without copying protected text.

supporting_sources.purpose: Accepted scientific names, authorship, ranks, family placement, and complete synonym resolution.
Stable external QIDs, English and Polish common names, and commercially safe licensed photos (CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA).
Mandatory Polish regulatory check for any amateur plant protection product mentioned in pest/disease protocols.

monstera_verified_baseline.watering: Allow top 2.5-5 cm (1-2 inches) of aerated substrate to dry before thorough watering with drainage; reduce frequency in winter.
monstera_verified_baseline.light_qualitative: Bright indirect light; tolerates gentle winter or early-morning sun in high latitudes; protect from direct summer midday sun unless acclimated.
monstera_verified_baseline.light_quantitative_interior: 100-150 FC (~1100-1600 lux) maintenance minimum; 150-250+ FC (~1600-2700+ lux) for good indoor vigor and fenestration (UF/IFAS interiorscape guidelines).
monstera_verified_baseline.substrate: Well-aerated peat/bark/perlite mix, pH 5.5-6.5, mandatory drainage hole.
monstera_verified_baseline.fertilizing: 3:1:2 NPK ratio balanced foliage fertilizer during active spring-summer growth; withhold in winter dormancy or root stress.
monstera_verified_baseline.safety_cats: toxic (insoluble calcium oxalate raphides — oral irritation, drooling, dysphagia; low systemic lethality)
monstera_verified_baseline.safety_dogs: toxic (insoluble calcium oxalate raphides — oral irritation, drooling, vomiting; low systemic lethality)

wikimedia_commons_filtered.basis: Allowed strictly for files under CC0, CC BY, and CC BY-SA with creator/license/modification attribution; exclude all CC BY-NC and CC BY-ND files.

us_university_extension_corpus.basis: 17 U.S.C. § 102(b) excludes scientific facts/measurements from copyright, whereas original prose and photos remain copyrighted by respective universities. Direct written confirmation recommended if storing raw HTML archives commercially.

aspca.basis: ASPCA Terms of Use prohibit commercial reproduction and automated scraping; underlying toxicological facts (e.g., presence of calcium oxalates) verified across veterinary sources are factual.

perenual.basis: Standard SaaS API terms grant active access rights rather than perpetual dataset buyout; enterprise contract quote required.

field_mapping.taxonomy: Kew WCVP (accepted taxon, rank, family, synonyms) + Wikidata (QID, EN/PL common names)
field_mapping.safety: Manual cross-verification of ASPCA (cat vs. dog) + NC State (toxic principle & clinical mechanism); Narat original EN/PL warning templates
field_mapping.care_algorithm_params: Botanical bounds (light FC/lux, temp min/opt, pH, NPK ratio, qualitative moisture strategy) from UF/IFAS + Extension; numeric day intervals and apartment modifiers modeled as Narat dynamic check-in heuristics
field_mapping.common_vulnerabilities: UF/IFAS host-pathogen tables + NC State / Extension species problem notes
field_mapping.care_content_i18n: Clean-room generated EN and PL structured guidance derived strictly from validated JSON fact matrices
field_mapping.provenance: Internal claim ledger tracking source_id, URL, publication date/version, SHA-256 snapshot hash, and reviewer sign-off per field

unresolved_conflicts.topic: Direct sunlight tolerance in Monstera deliciosa and tropical foliage plants
unresolved_conflicts.explanation: Apparent conflict between 'no direct sun' (NC State outdoor/southern US context) and 'gentle winter/morning direct sun allowed' (northern indoor Extension context). Resolved by splitting seasonal/latitude and acclimation attributes rather than averaging.

unresolved_conflicts.topic: Taxonomic synonym lag in toxicology databases
unresolved_conflicts.explanation: ASPCA and older horticultural guides list Sansevieria trifasciata or Calathea spp., whereas Kew WCVP places them in Dracaena and Goeppertia. Resolved via mandatory WCVP synonym expansion before matching.

missing_data: Scientifically universal watering intervals in exact days (physically dependent on pot volume, substrate porosity, VPD, and season).
Empirically proven numeric multipliers for terracotta pots, heating radiators, and window distance.
Exact recovery timelines in days for root rot or pest eradication (must be represented as observation check-in windows).
Species-by-species peer-reviewed protocols for semi-hydroponics (LECA/pon) across all 300 indoor taxa.
Visual-only definitive diagnosis for microscopic broad mites, systemic viruses, and root-zone pH lockouts without user physical checks.

spec_conflicts.rule: Minimum 2 independent sources for numeric recommendations
spec_conflicts.conflict: Quantitative interior light ranges (FC/lux) for foliage plants originate primarily from one foundational experimental research body (UF/IFAS Apopka trials); secondary sites merely copy those numbers.
spec_conflicts.proposed_resolution: Extend the authoritative single-source exception in Narat's specification to cover peer-reviewed experimental physiological measurements (lux/FC, pH, EC) when cited directly from primary academic publications.
